stories.headline: Analog Devices nears $1.5B all-cash deal for AI power-chip startup Empower Semiconductor

key_facts.fact: Analog Devices is in advanced talks to acquire Empower Semiconductor for approximately $1.5 billion in cash, with an announcement possible as early as Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Semiconductor manufacturer Analog Devices is reportedly in advanced discussions to acquire AI-focused chipmaker Empower Semiconductor. The deal is estimated to be worth approximately $1.5 billion in cash... The acquisition could be announced as early as Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Empower designs integrated voltage regulator ICs (the Crescendo family) that sit directly under GPUs and other AI accelerators, delivering more than 3,000 amps to AI processors.
key_facts.excerpt: Empower tries to solve some of the challenges with traditional power electronics with its latest family of voltage-regulator ICs called Crescendo. The technology relocates the active power delivery directly under the GPU or other AI accelerator, slinging more than 3,000 A of current up through the PCB instead of across it.

key_facts.fact: The deal would extend Analog Devices' acquisition streak — the company has done 16 acquisitions over the past decade, including the $20.9B Maxim Integrated takeout in 2021 and Flex Logix in November 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: This acquisition would follow the company's recent acquisition of Flex Logix in November 2024... In 2021, Analog Devices completed its landmark $20.9 billion acquisition of Maxim Integrated... Over the past decade, the company has completed 16 acquisitions.

key_facts.fact: Empower's solutions are already deployed in high-performance computing environments, and the acquisition aligns with ADI's push into AI infrastructure power management.
key_facts.excerpt: Empower specializes in advanced power management and integrated voltage regulator technology, which aims to reduce energy loss, improve processing efficiency, and increase computing density. The company's solutions are already being used in high-performance computing environments.

stories.headline: Anthropic Acquires Stainless, Reportedly Over $300M, to Pull SDK Tooling From Rival Labs

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced on May 18, 2026 it has acquired Stainless, the dev-tools startup whose software generates SDKs for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare, Replicate and Runway.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Anthropic is acquiring Stainless, a leader in SDKs and MCP server tooling, to extend that reach even further. Founded in 2022, Stainless has powered the generation of every official Anthropic SDK since the earliest days of our API.

key_facts.fact: Terms were not disclosed, but The Information previously reported Anthropic was in talks to buy Stainless for more than $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic didn't disclose terms of the deal. However, The Information reported last week that the company was in talks to acquire Stainless, which is backed by Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, for more than $300 million.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told TechCrunch it will wind down all hosted Stainless products including the SDK generator; existing customers keep rights to SDKs already generated.
key_facts.excerpt: The company told TechCrunch it will wind down all hosted Stainless products, including its SDK generator. An Anthropic spokesperson said Stainless customers will still own the SDKs they've generated to date and have full rights to modify and extend them however they wish.

key_facts.fact: Stainless was founded in 2022 by former Stripe engineer Alex Rattray and is backed by Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced Monday it has acquired Stainless, a startup founded by former Stripe engineer Alex Rattray whose software is widely used by rival AI labs, including OpenAI and Google.

key_facts.fact: Stainless turns API specs into native SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin and other languages, plus MCP server tooling.
key_facts.excerpt: Stainless turns an API spec into SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, and more. Each one is fast, reliable, and built to feel native in its language.

stories.headline: Intel pushes US/China/Taiwan PC makers to use more 18A CPUs amid AI-driven supply crunch

key_facts.fact: Intel is asking leading PC partners in the US, China and Taiwan to increase use of CPUs built with its 18A process, citing better supply than older-node chips, Nikkei Asia reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel is pushing notebook and PC manufacturers to adopt central processing units built with its most advanced chip production technology as surging demand for AI computing power strains supplies of the key component, Nikkei Asia reported on Tuesday. The chipmaker is asking leading PC partners in the U.S., China and Taiwan to increase their use of CPUs built with the company's 18A production process.

key_facts.fact: Intel specifically cited better supply on its Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake CPU lines, which run on 18A, versus older-node parts.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel told partners that supply of cutting-edge CPUs, specifically the Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake lines, is better than that of processors based on older chipmaking technologies, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: CEO Lip-Bu Tan said separately on Monday that Intel expects 'multiple' external foundry customer commitments in the second half of the year, with 18A improvements drawing growing customer interest.
key_facts.excerpt: Tan pointed to improvements in Intel's advanced 18A manufacturing process... The improvements are beginning to draw customer interest, according to Tan... Tan said Intel expects commitments from multiple foundry customers in the second half of the year. 'Multiple customers, they are working with us,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Intel has built a new 18A plant in Arizona, while a separate Ohio project has faced major delays and is not expected to start production until at least 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has built a new plant in Arizona, where it uses the 18A process, while a separate project in Ohio has faced major delays and isn't set to start production until at least 2030.

stories.headline: Iran unveils 'Hormuz Safe' Bitcoin-backed shipping insurance for Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Iran's Ministry of Economy has launched 'Hormuz Safe,' a digital insurance platform that issues marine insurance policies for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz with payments settled in Bitcoin, per Fars News Agency reporting on May 18.
key_facts.excerpt: State-linked Fars News reported that Iran's economy ministry has been working on a plan to manage shipping through the Strait using marine insurance policies and financial responsibility certificates, with payments settled in bitcoin.

key_facts.fact: Officials project the platform could generate more than $10 billion in revenue for Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials involved in the project estimate that the platform could eventually generate more than $10 billion in revenue for Iran, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: Policies would cover risks such as cargo inspection, detention, and confiscation — but exclude damages from weapon strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan would start with insurance covering risks such as inspection, detention, and confiscation, excluding damages from weapon strikes.

key_facts.fact: About 20% of the world's crude oil and LNG supplies flowed through Hormuz before the US-Iran war began Feb. 28, 2026; the strait has been mostly closed since.
key_facts.excerpt: About 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas supplies flowed through Hormuz prior to the war.

key_facts.fact: Any use of Hormuz Safe would create sanctions-compliance risk for shipowners, traders and insurers because payments would flow to Iranian state-linked entities.
key_facts.excerpt: Because payments to Iranian state-linked entities can trigger sanctions exposure, any use of Hormuz Safe would pose significant compliance risks for shipowners, traders and insurers, and the platform's operational status remains unverified.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Arkham reported Iran's largest crypto exchange Nobitex has processed more than $2.3 billion since 2023 via Tron and BNB Chain, including over $23 million since the Iran war started in February.

stories.headline: Kia to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid first in Georgia assembly plants

key_facts.fact: Kia President Song Ho-sung said on Monday during overseas non-deal roadshow meetings in Singapore and Hong Kong that the company plans to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot first in difficult and physically demanding assembly processes.
key_facts.excerpt: Kia President Song Ho-sung said the company plans to deploy the humanoid robot Atlas first in difficult and physically demanding assembly processes at its factories. Song made the remarks during overseas non-deal roadshow meetings in Singapore and Hong Kong, industry sources said Monday.

key_facts.fact: Atlas will be deployed first at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia, and a year later at Kia's Georgia plant, because the production systems and factory structures are the same.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Atlas will first be deployed at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia, and a year later at Kia's Georgia plant,' Song said. 'Because the production systems and factory structures are the same, once Atlas can be used in one production process, it can be applied the same way at other plants.'

key_facts.fact: Hyundai Motor Group is building a humanoid mass production system with annual capacity of 30,000 units by 2028, with deployments at Hyundai Metaplant America starting in 2028 and at Kia's Georgia plant in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Hyundai Motor is building a mass production system for humanoid robots with an annual capacity of 30,000 units by 2028. The company plans to begin deploying humanoids at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in 2028 and at Kia's Georgia plant in 2029.

key_facts.fact: The disclosure also raised speculation about a potential IPO for Boston Dynamics, the US robotics company owned by Hyundai Motor Group.
key_facts.excerpt: The possible deployment of Atlas has also drawn attention to whether Boston Dynamics, the U.S. robotics company owned by Hyundai Motor Group, could pursue an initial public offering.

stories.headline: Jury Unanimously Rejects Musk's $150B Lawsuit Against OpenAI After Two-Hour Deliberation

key_facts.fact: A nine-person California jury unanimously rejected Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman on May 18, 2026, finding the suit fell outside the statute of limitations.
key_facts.excerpt: A California jury on Monday unanimously dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman on the grounds that Musk had failed to file a claim within the statute of limitations.

key_facts.fact: Jurors deliberated about two hours after a three-week trial that included testimony from Musk, Altman, Greg Brockman and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.
key_facts.excerpt: Jurors spent just about two hours on Monday deliberating on the case, but they had spent three weeks viewing internal correspondence and hearing testimony from Musk, Altman and other tech industry executives, such as Microsoft's chief executive Satya Nadella.

key_facts.fact: Musk had sought $150 billion in damages and Altman's removal; the verdict removes a major obstacle to OpenAI's planned IPO at an $852B valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk was seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and Altman's removal from company leadership. A decision in Musk's favor could also have forced changes to OpenAI's business structure and thrown a wrench into the company's plan to go public, expected later this year.

key_facts.fact: Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers accepted the advisory jury's verdict and dismissed the claims; Musk's separate claims against Microsoft were dismissed as a matter of law.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk's other claims against Microsoft were dismissed as a matter of law given the jury's findings on the two claims against OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Musk's lawyer William Savitt said the jury 'decided that Musk was lying during his testimony about the company's origins'; Musk said he will appeal to the Ninth Circuit.
key_facts.excerpt: an appeal with the Ninth [...] to charitable giving in America.

stories.headline: NextEra to buy Dominion for $67B in largest US utility deal, citing AI power demand

key_facts.fact: NextEra Energy agreed to acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock deal valued at about $67 billion, the largest power acquisition in US history, creating the world's largest regulated electric utility.
key_facts.excerpt: NextEra Energy said Monday it will acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock deal valued at about $67 billion... The all-stock transaction will create the 'largest regulated electric utility' in the world, the companies said Monday.

key_facts.fact: NextEra shareholders will own about 74.5% of the combined company; Dominion shareholders 25.5%. The merged utility will serve about 10 million customers across Florida, Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina.
key_facts.excerpt: NextEra Energy shareholders will own approximately 74.5% of the company while Dominion shareholders will own 25.5%. The combined company, which will operate under the name NextEra Energy, will serve around 10 million utility customers across Florida, Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina.

key_facts.fact: NextEra and Dominion together have roughly 130 GW of contracted data-center demand seeking grid connection, with Dominion alone holding nearly 51 GW of contracted data-center capacity from Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal will enable a swifter build-out of power infrastructure to deliver electricity to data centres proposing to connect to NextEra and Dominion, which total about 130 gigawatts of electricity demand, the companies' executives said... Virginia-based [Dominion] has nearly 51 gigawatts of contracted data-centre capacity.

key_facts.fact: The companies pledged $2.25 billion in customer credits over two years to Dominion ratepayers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina as part of the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of the deal, the companies said they would offer Dominion customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina a total of $2.25 billion in credits over two years.

key_facts.fact: US utilities and grid operators are expected to invest more than $1.1 trillion over the next five years on new generation and transmission projects.

stories.headline: Seagate plunges nearly 7% as CEO rules out new factories, drags memory chip stocks down

key_facts.fact: Seagate shares closed down about 6.9% on Monday, leading a sector-wide sell-off, after CEO Dave Mosley said at the JPMorgan Global Technology, Media and Communications Conference that building new factories would 'take too long.'
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of memory chip maker Seagate closed down more than 6% Monday, leading a group-wide sell-off, after comments from CEO Dave Mosley raised concerns that it won't be able to meet the soaring demand fueled by the artificial intelligence buildout.

key_facts.fact: Mosley said critical components like recording head wafers have lead times exceeding nine months, with drives taking an additional quarter, and that demand 'significantly exceeds' current supply.

key_facts.fact: Seagate is targeting mid-20s percent CAGR by advancing from 3 TB-per-platter to 4 and 5 TB-per-platter products rather than greenfield capacity additions, with Q3 non-GAAP gross margin hitting an all-time high of 47.0%.

stories.headline: Standard Chartered to cut ~7,800 back-office roles by 2030 as it scales AI automation

key_facts.excerpt: Standard Chartered on Tuesday announced it would cut more than 15% of its corporate functions roles by 2030, while setting higher medium-term profitability targets.

key_facts.fact: The cuts target back-office functions including HR, risk, compliance and supply chain; about 52,000 of StanChart's roughly 82,000 employees work in support roles per the 2025 annual report.
key_facts.excerpt: According to its 2025 annual report, corporate function roles include employees in human resources, corporate affairs and supply chain management. Of its roughly 82,000 employees, about 52,000 work in support roles.

key_facts.fact: The bank aims to raise income per employee by about 20% by 2028 and target a 15% return on tangible equity in 2028, rising to roughly 18% by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The workforce reduction is part of the lender's efforts to raise income per employee by around 20% by 2028... The lender also aimed for a 15% return on tangible equity in 2028, up more than three percentage points from 2025, and targeted about 18% in 2030.

key_facts.fact: StanChart has major back-office operations in India, China, Malaysia and Poland; the company said it would try to redeploy some affected workers.
key_facts.excerpt: The company did not give details of where the roles would be cut. It has major back-office operations in India, China, Malaysia and Poland... The BBC understands that Standard Chartered aims to move some of the affected workers to other roles in the business.

stories.headline: Tenstorrent draws early takeover interest from Intel and Qualcomm at $5B+ valuation

key_facts.fact: AI chip designer Tenstorrent has held early-stage takeover conversations with industry players including Intel and Qualcomm, according to Bloomberg sources.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence chip startup Tenstorrent Inc. is drawing early takeover interest from prospective buyers at a moment of renewed momentum for upstarts looking to challenge Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Tenstorrent, which designs chips that it says are more efficient at running certain AI workloads, has held conversations with industry players including Intel Corp. and Qualcomm Inc., according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Tenstorrent could be valued at more than $5 billion in a potential deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: AI chip designer Tenstorrent has drawn takeover interest from Intel and Qualcomm; Tenstorrent could be valued at more than $5B in a potential deal (Bloomberg)

key_facts.fact: Tenstorrent, led by veteran chip designer Jim Keller, was raising $800m at a $3.2bn pre-money valuation in November 2025, up from a $693m Series D closed in December 2024 at $2.6bn.
key_facts.excerpt: Tenstorrent, an AI chip startup led by Jim Keller, has reportedly held early-stage takeover discussions with Intel and Qualcomm, as it seeks to raise $800m at a $3.2bn pre-money valuation in November 2025, up from the $693m Series D it closed in December 2024 at $2.6bn.

key_facts.fact: The company designs RISC-V-based AI accelerators (Ascalon CPU cores and Tensix AI cores) sold both as packaged silicon and as licensable IP — a hybrid model that distinguishes it from pure chip startups.
key_facts.excerpt: The company designs RISC-V-based AI accelerators (Ascalon CPU cores and Tensix AI cores) that are sold both as packaged silicon and as licensable IP, a hybrid model for a chip startup.

key_facts.fact: Existing Tenstorrent investors include Bezos Expeditions, LG Electronics, Baillie Gifford, Hyundai Motor Group, Samsung Securities, AFW Partners, Fidelity, and the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Securities and AFW Partners led the round. Jeff Bezos' Bezos Expeditions, Fidelity Management & Research Co. and LG Electronics also joined the funding for Tenstorrent... Export Development Canada, Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan, Hyundai Motor Group, Baillie Gifford and other investors also participated in the deal.

stories.headline: Trump postpones planned Tuesday Iran attack at request of Saudi, UAE, Qatar leaders

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on May 18 he was 'holding off' a scheduled Tuesday attack on Iran after the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar asked for a pause to allow negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump said Monday that he will 'hold off' on a Tuesday plan to attack Iran, citing a request from the leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates as he said negotiations to end the war grow more 'serious.'

key_facts.fact: Trump instructed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to be ready for a 'full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice' if no acceptable deal is reached.
key_facts.excerpt: The president said he told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine that while Tuesday's attack is off, they should 'be prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice, in the event that an acceptable Deal is not reached.'

key_facts.fact: Iran on May 18 conveyed its response to Washington's latest proposal through mediator Pakistan, per Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a press briefing on Monday that Tehran's response to the latest US proposal had been 'conveyed to the American side through mediator Pakistan.'

key_facts.fact: Washington's five-point proposal reportedly demands Iran keep only one nuclear site operational and transfer its highly enriched uranium stockpile to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian news agency Fars reported on Sunday that Washington had presented a five-point list, which made it clear the US would cease hostilities only when Tehran engages in formal peace negotiations. It also included a demand for Iran to keep only one nuclear site in operation and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to the US.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose more than 2% to settle at $112.10 a barrel on May 18, while WTI rose ~3% to $108.66, before easing in extended trading on news of the postponement.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures rose more than 2% to close at $112.10 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for June advanced about 3% to settle at $108.66 per barrel. But prices eased in extended trading with Brent dipping back below $110.

key_facts.fact: The IEA warned global oil inventories are 'depleting at a record pace' with cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceeding 1 billion barrels and more than 14 mb/d shut in.
key_facts.excerpt: With Hormuz tanker traffic still restricted, cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceed 1 billion barrels with more than 14 mb/d of oil now shut in, an unprecedented supply shock.

stories.headline: Vatican Sets May 25 Release of Pope Leo's First Encyclical on AI, With Anthropic's Olah on Stage

key_facts.fact: The Vatican announced on May 18, 2026 that Pope Leo XIV will release his first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, on May 25 covering the protection of human dignity in the age of AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The Vatican announced Monday that Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical will be published on May 25, with the title Magnifica Humanitas. [...] the full title of the encyclical is Magnifica Humanitas: On the Protection of Human Dignity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic co-founder Christopher Olah will join the pope, Curial cardinals and theologians at the May 25 presentation in the Vatican's Synod Hall.
key_facts.excerpt: The encyclical, titled Magnifica Humanitas ('Magnificent Humanity'), will center on 'the protection of the human person in the age of artificial intelligence' and will be presented May 25 by the pope as well as Curial cardinals and theologians, the Vatican announced Monday. [...] To that end, among those joining him will be Christopher Olah, a co-founder of Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Leo signed the encyclical on May 15, 135 years to the day after Leo XIII signed Rerum Novarum on workers' rights during the Industrial Revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV signed his first encyclical on May 15, a document on the protection of the human person in the age of artificial intelligence, the Vatican announced today. His signature came on the 135th anniversary of the promulgation of Pope Leo XIII's famous encyclical 'Rerum Novarum'.

key_facts.fact: Speakers include Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, Cardinal Michael Czerny, Professor Anna Rowlands of Durham, Olah, and Professor Leocadie Lushombo of Santa Clara University.
key_facts.excerpt: The speakers at the encyclical's presentation will be: Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith; Cardinal Michael Czerny, SJ, prefect of the Dicastery for Integral Human Development; Anna Rowlands, professor of ethics and political theology at the University of Durham in the United Kingdom; Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic USA; and Léocadie Lushombo.

key_facts.fact: On May 16 the Vatican announced the creation of a cross-dicasteries AI study group covering Holy See policies on AI use.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the weekend (May 16), the Vatican announced the creation of a study group on AI working across various dicasteries to exchange information on projects related to artificial intelligence 'including policies on its use within the Holy See.'
